new.meaning: “the nūn of protection”: the nūn between a verb and the speaker's <bdi>ي</bdi>, as in <bdi>ضَرَبَنِي</bdi>
new.source: Tasheel al-Nahw ch.2 — class notes to 2026-10-23

new.front: Why does a verb take a nūn before the speaker's <bdi>ي</bdi>, as in <bdi>ضَرَبَنِي</bdi>?
new.back: The <bdi>ي</bdi> needs a kasrah before it, and a verb can't take a kasrah. So <bdi>نُون الوِقَايَة</bdi> is added to carry it, protecting the verb's own ending.
new.source: Tasheel al-Nahw ch.2 — class notes to 2026-10-23

new.front: What are <bdi>ضَمِير الشَّأْن</bdi> and <bdi>ضَمِير القِصَّة</bdi>, and how do they differ from ordinary pronouns?
new.back: The same pronoun, masculine (<bdi>الشَّأْن</bdi>) and feminine (<bdi>القِصَّة</bdi>). Ordinary pronouns refer back to something already mentioned; these refer ahead, to the sentence that follows: <bdi>إِنَّهُ لَا يُفْلِحُ الظَّالِمُونَ</bdi>.
new.source: Tasheel al-Nahw ch.2 — class notes to 2026-10-23

new.meaning: “the pronoun of separation”: a pronoun between the mubtadaʾ and the khabar, for emphasis and separation — <bdi>أُولَٰئِكَ هُمُ المُفْلِحُونَ</bdi>
new.source: Tasheel al-Nahw ch.2 — class notes to 2026-10-23

new.meaning: a relative pronoun — it can't form a complete part of the sentence without its ṣilah
new.source: Tasheel al-Nahw ch.2 — class notes to 2026-10-23

new.meaning: the clause that completes an ism mawṣūl — generally a jumlah khabariyyah, with a pronoun referring back to it
new.source: Tasheel al-Nahw ch.2 — class notes to 2026-10-23

new.meaning: the pronoun in the ṣilah that refers back to the ism mawṣūl — it can be bāriz or mustatir
new.source: Tasheel al-Nahw ch.2 — class notes to 2026-10-23

new.text:
مُفْرَدمُثَنًّىجَمْع
مُذَكَّر{{c1::الَّذِي}}{{c2::اللَّذَانِ / اللَّذَيْنِ}}{{c3::الَّذِينَ}}
مُؤَنَّث{{c4::الَّتِي}}{{c5::اللَّتَانِ / اللَّتَيْنِ}}{{c6::اللَّاتِي / اللَّوَاتِي}}
new.extra: The relative pronouns. The duals change with iʿrāb: <bdi>اللَّذَانِ</bdi> and <bdi>اللَّتَانِ</bdi> in rafʿ, <bdi>اللَّذَيْنِ</bdi> and <bdi>اللَّتَيْنِ</bdi> in naṣb and jarr. The rest are mabnī.
new.source: Tasheel al-Nahw ch.2 — class notes to 2026-10-23

new.front: Which relative pronouns serve every gender and number, and how are they divided?
new.back: <bdi>مَنْ</bdi>, for intelligent beings, and <bdi>مَا</bdi>, for non-intelligent ones
new.source: Tasheel al-Nahw ch.2 — class notes to 2026-10-23

new.front: Which two relative pronouns are formed from <bdi>أَيّ</bdi>, and what do they mean?
new.source: Tasheel al-Nahw ch.2 — class notes to 2026-10-23

new.front: What effect does al- have before an ism fāʿil or ism mafʿūl?
new.back: It works like an ism mawṣūl: <bdi>الضَّارِبُ</bdi> means <bdi>الَّذِي ضَرَبَ</bdi>, “the one who struck”
new.source: Tasheel al-Nahw ch.2 — class notes to 2026-10-23
